label: copy-phase input s (fed-back s), mid/late recall, next output in {s,v,w,i,d,n,x,l,u}
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase and almost only when the input token is s, the model echoing back an s it just output (99.4% of activation mass is on in_tok = s). It never fires in the original or delimiter phases. Copy-phase s alone has 98% recall but only 17% precision, since most fed-back s steps stay silent. Activity is concentrated at recall_idx 3-6 (t 10-14) and is near zero for recall_idx <= 2. Which token is being output next matters a lot: rate is highest when out_tok is s, v, i, w or d, then n, x, l, u. Restricting to that set gives dev F1 0.62 with mass recall 0.78. Rate also rises with longer L and with repeated s (in_count >= 2). The largest activations come from the first fed-back s in a run, early in the copy phase (recall 3-4), e.g. q l h s w; later repeats of s are weaker. It does not fire on fed-back w or v (under 0.5% of mass) or on s in the original sequence. Residual precision is incomplete: many s inputs that match the predicate stay silent, probably because of hidden-state context this predicate does not capture.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: s, w, v, d, i, m; least: 3, y, f, 0) and the token being output (most: s, v, w, i, d, n; least: o, g, e, -); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=4, recall_idx=3, t=12.
